title: The comment asks to defer the default CA load to first verified use and says that, with certs.where() naming a missing or unreadable file, import requests now fails with FileNotFoundError, where the base failed only a default-verified request with a clear OSError.

reproduced.base: With the default CA file missing, import succeeds; plain HTTP, verify=False, verify=<CA file> and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE return 200; default verify raises OSError naming the missing path at the request (probes/C1n/result-base.txt).
reproduced.head: import requests raises FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory from adapters.py line 76, so every case fails (probes/C1n/result-head.txt).

not_run: a real distribution image without its CA package; the missing file was simulated by repointing certifi.where() or by a certifi package placed first on the path
strongest_argument_against: GT-i2's answer key already lists an error raised straight out of `import requests` by this same load_verify_locations call (PermissionError, #6764) as one of GT-i2's results, so a comment saying the import now fails because of the eager load says what goes wrong for GT-i2 on its present wording and recovers without waiting for the C1n grouping ruling.

facts.note: Identifies the cause as a fault: yes; the claim field's 'Defer loading the default CA bundle until first verified use' names GT-i2's cause, the load at import (adapters.py 75-78), and asks for it to change, and the consequence ties the failure to 'module import' (read). Says what goes wrong: cannot tell; the import failure on a missing file is true (run) and comes from the same call as GT-i2's recorded PermissionError, but GT-i2's wording holds only the zip-archive setup and import cost; it is yes if the owner joins C1n to GT-i2 and no if C1n stays separate (rule Before 4). The unreadable case raises PermissionError at import, not the FileNotFoundError the consequence names (run).

ran: Ran import, plain HTTP, verify=False, verify=<CA file>, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and default-verify cases at base and head with Python 3.12.14, urllib3 2.2.1 and certifi 2024.2.2, with certifi.where() repointed to a missing file and with a distribution-style certifi: the base imports, serves every non-default case and raises 'Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle, invalid path: <path>' only for default verify; the head raises FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory from adapters.py line 76 at import in every case.
Repeated at base and head with Python 3.13.15, urllib3 2.8.0 and certifi 2026.07.22: the same results.

Ran the unreadable-file case (mode 000, non-root user) at base and head: the base imports and serves HTTP and verify=False, and default verify raises SSLError caused by PermissionError; the head raises PermissionError at import.

Ran the comment's proposed shape (fix-both-verify-true: a cached helper called from _urllib3_request_context for verify=True, raising the base's OSError) at head: import and verify=False work, default verify raises the OSError, and a plain http:// request also raises it because http:// requests carry verify=True; the https-only form (fix-both) serves plain HTTP.

title: With no file at the default CA location (a packager's where() pointing at an absent system file, or a stripped environment), import requests raises FileNotFoundError at the head, so plain HTTP, verify=False, verify=<own file> and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE are all lost; before the change they worked and only a default-verified request failed, with a message naming the path.
rule_gap: Rule Before 4 asks whether one fix cures both; it does not say what follows when the shared fix (deferring the load) cures both and a narrower guard (catching FileNotFoundError) cures this group alone and leaves GT-i2 standing, the shape in which the owner kept GT-i9 apart from GT-i2 in first-round ruling 34, made under an earlier reading.

promise.whose_interface: requests: `import requests`, the documented verify=False, verify=<path> and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, and the default CA location requests.certs.where(), which is certifi.where() unless a packager redefines it as src/requests/certs.py invites.
promise.source: docs/user/advanced.rst line 241: "Requests can also ignore verifying the SSL certificate if you set ``verify`` to False::"; line 226: "You can pass ``verify`` the path to a CA_BUNDLE file or directory with certificates of trusted CAs::"; line 238: "This list of trusted CAs can also be specified through the ``REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`` environment variable."; src/requests/certs.py lines 10-12: "If you are packaging Requests, e.g., for a Linux distribution or a managed environment, you can change the definition of where() to return a separately packaged CA bundle." None of these uses needs the default file, and at the base they worked without it (rule Promised 7a).

One fix: fix-lazy (the load moved to a helper for https:// verify=True requests) cures every failing case of both: no load during import (0 calls; import self time 322 us against 6339 us at head and 347 us at base), the zip-case PermissionError, and the missing-file import, plain HTTP, verify=False, verify=<file> and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; only the base's message for a default-verified request with the file missing is not restored (FileNotFoundError without the path at the request), and fix-both restores it. fix-guard (catch FileNotFoundError at import) cures this group and none of GT-i2's cases. One sentence: GT-i2's own cause sentence, 'The module-level block runs load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)) on import.', is true of both.
